lines: I never actually needed it, since I never used more than two or three GB, but now I just upload 30 GB so I can say I use it.

The stupid thing is I always said "no SaaS subscriptions", then October 2026 came and I ended up with two: OneDrive 100 GB and Muse Code for 4,29 €/mo. Back in April 2026 I predicted — and tagged Meta — that they should ship a $5/month tier with a lot of tokens: https://x.com/d5_iel/status/2113593415564771351 — and they actually did. Honest take though: I would have subscribed to whichever lab shipped a ~$5 tier first.

Muse Code itself is surprisingly good: it's terminal-only and the UX is a bit bad, but it has really useful features and the syntax highlighting is genuinely nice, and the Everyday tier is enough for a ton of work. I did have to add some strict personal memory settings to not burn a ton of tokens: single session only — never use subagents, observers or multiple sessions, verify everything myself in the main thread; save tokens, be concise, avoid parallel exploration; stop after 1–2 failed attempts on the same task and escalate with what was tried, the exact blocking error and what's needed instead of retrying variants, treating repeated tool failures, permission denials or unchanged output as a hard stop; and default to writing code/files only — never run, test, verify, execute, install or set up environments (no Python/Node/NPM installs, no builds, no test runs, no servers) unless I give explicit approval first.

-Long term I don't want just any job, I want to build my own thing and found an IT company for hosting, infrastructure and IT consulting, based on infra-pilot (https://github.com/drosemann/infra-pilot).

+Long term I don't want just any job, I want to build my own thing and found an IT company for hosting, infrastructure and IT consulting, based on infra-pilot (https://github.com/drosemann/infra-pilot), my Docker-native infrastructure control plane for my own VPS and container fleet with a React and Express management panel, a Python orchestrator agent with GitOps reconciliation, a Typer-based ipilot CLI and optional Discord and monitoring profiles.
I want scalable cloud solutions instead of generic root servers, built on pure Docker and KVM.
I also want to buy an old house, make it smart the cheap way, and document all of it on YouTube.
I want to share what I learn, so a YouTube channel about IT and hosting is planned.
